incident.close_notes: Design team locked out of the Lucidchart app - RESOLVED. The design org reported they could no longer open Lucidchart through the SSO tile, though it kept working for one lead who had been set up individually. The same-day diagramming-connector patch was suspected and nearly rolled back; on inspection the app itself was healthy and still served that one directly-entitled lead, so the patch was NOT the cause. A quarterly access review the night before had over-reached on the design org's entitlements: it had removed the design group's assignment from the app, dropped several designers out of that group, put a few active designers into a suspended state, cleared some people's MFA enrollment, and reclaimed a batch of the app's paid licenses as 'unused'. We compared the design org against a healthy peer app and its group, then restored each layer for exactly the affected people - re-attached the group to the app and re-added the dropped members (never opening the app to everyone), reactivated the wrongly-suspended accounts, restored their sign-in factor, and re-granted the specific paid license the rest of the entitled group still held. Contractors the review had genuinely offboarded were left deactivated. The suspected connector patch was left untouched. Lesson: verify the reported cause, don't trust a 'works for one person' spot-check, restore the WHOLE entitlement chain for the intended cohort only, least privilege, and don't resurrect deactivated leavers. Closed.

incident.short_description: Design team locked out of Lucidchart - blamed on a connector patch, was an access-review over-reach

incident.description:
Since first thing this morning our analytics team cannot open their Power BI dashboards - the SSO tile either errors out or the reports fail to load. It is affecting the team broadly, though a couple of people say it still works for them. A few of the affected people also report that after their password they are now stuck at the extra sign-in verification - the prompt never reaches their phone, and the portal gives them no way to set that back up themselves, so IT will have to sort that out for them as part of this.
Suspected cause: the Power BI SAML connector update that was pushed last night (change CHG0044001). Please confirm whether that update broke it and get the analytics team back into Power BI.
Investigate across the available systems, confirm the actual root cause before making changes, restore access for the correct people, and close this incident once the analytics team can get into Power BI again.
incident.short_description: Analytics team cannot access Power BI (since this morning)
